title: Australian Museum, Sydney
geometryBasis: The named OpenStreetMap building outline fixes the 111 m by about 71 m irregular footprint with the projecting Barnet front, turn into College Street, and the distinct Crystal Hall projection and entrance. Post-construction reports distinguish the historic U-shaped wings, covered yard, Parkes Farmer and the newer eastern building masses.
sectionBasis: Pickering’s 1872 published view gives the retained College Street giant Corinthian order, plinth, three axial bays, and hipped wing pavilions. NSW Public Works gives the sandstone and the storey arrangement. The 2013 and 2022 CC0 photographs provide the Parkes Farmer windowless wing and the Crystal Hall glazing. Construction and design reports give the crystal entry dimensions, offset and raised access, and Qualla’s original confirms the covered former courtyard.
limitations: Standing post-2020 exterior at College and William Streets. The map determines the building perimeter. Cornice, gable, internal wing divisions, roof appurtenances, old window and relief details, and exact site grade have reconstructed dimensions.

The nearly 20 by 8 m Crystal Hall and 4.5 m Museum Walk follow the design and published perimeter. The translucent diamond colors and steel framing are geometric approximations to the cleared architectural image. The known decorative artwork on other modern walls is outside the geometric reconstruction.

The frozen 256 m original site elevation field is used for terrain review. Modern foundations and lower wings follow its falling grade east and north with estimated footing depths. The model includes the mapped linked museum block. Adjacent Sydney Grammar School and detached structures are outside the exterior scope.
